record.title: Togo April 2024 legislative and regional election land-border closure
record.scope: National land-border closure ordered for polling day
record.crossings: National order; resumed movement reported specifically at Aflao and Hilacondji
record.direction: National land restriction; later Aflao account explicitly describes entries and exits.
record.movement: Land-border users and cross-border movement; exact goods-category treatment not specified.
record.exceptions: Airport and seaport remained open; no land-category exemption located in the retrieved communiqué.
record.imposing_authority: Togolese ministers of Territorial Administration and Security
record.enforcement: Order is explicit; reopening reporting describes ordinary movements at two named posts, without precise first-passage times.
record.consequences: Temporary interruption to cross-border activities; no quantified losses adopted.
record.relationship: Different polling event from W-026 (2018), SUP-002 (2019), SUP-003 (2025), and the explicitly nonclosed February 2020 presidential election SUP-L01.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Secure the legislative and regional vote and maintain public order.
record.context: Joint ministerial decision announced on 27 April scheduled the closure for polling day. Later reports describe traffic restored the following morning.
record.uncertainty: The planned window ended at 23:59 on 29 April. Actual traffic is reported on 30 April at named crossings, not individually verified at every post. Two reopening articles share distinctive details; independence is not assumed.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. National order has an exact schedule, but the operational endpoint is observed in reporting at selected crossings only; no all-post continuous duration supplied.
